independent_outcomes: Not-clean status spreads along plain `Depends on` edges between finished ids, so a finished id built on a not-clean finished id is held and named with its cause, and the rest of the run goes on. This covers success clauses 1 and 3 (the one-hop case and the chain).
proposed_seams: No split proposed. The four success clauses are one defect seen at different depths: clause 1 is the one-hop case, clause 3 is the same rule applied transitively, and clause 2 (#624's U -> D -> E) is that same rule one level up. Clause 2 cannot ship alone, because its test passes only with the same flow.py hunk that clause 1 needs.
The docs sentence (docs/07-crosscutting.md:686-691) and the _carry_finished docstring (flow.py:883-885) describe the new behaviour, so they ship in the same PR. They are not a separate outcome.
The fold-time residual (a finished id whose merge fails during the fold) is already excluded by the brief. It is a separate, larger change, not a seam to cut now.
